Prevention: Plough the land deep (92-152cm) to improve drainage and aeration before planting.
Soil solarization with black polythene sheets before planting.
Apply organic mulches and inorganic gypsum to the soil to prevent rot disease.
Plant disease free seedlings from certified nurseries.
Do not move soil from diseased orchards 3
Do not work in infested ochards when the soil is wet as phytophthora is readily spread by walking or driving on infested soil.
Disinfect tools with 2.5%JIK after working on each tree.
Begin harvesting and other activities in healthy parts of the orchard, work in diseased areas last to minimize disease movement.
Monitoring: This is a water mould disease spread by infected seedlings, soil, water runoff and infected tools.
Do regular visits in the orchard especially when the trees are young (fortnightly).
Check the tips of leaves and shoots, check for small pale green or yellowish leaves which often wilt and have necrotic tips.
Look under the trees, there may be prematurely dropped leaves under infected trees.

Remove a bit of soil and check for roots that are small, black, brittle and dead at an advanced stage of the disease.
It’s too late for chemical control when several avocado trees are infected.
Direct Control: TV at the rate of 500grams in 100 litres of water (100-200 grams per m3) as a drench around on young trees showing early symptoms.
Restrictions: When using a pesticide or botanical, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage, timing of application, pre-harvest interval, max number of sprays, restricted re- entry interval.
